name: TA416 Group Targets Government and Diplomatic Networks
description: Attackers are targeting government and diplomatic organizations in Europe and the Middle East using phishing emails, web bugs and trusted cloud services. This campaign delivers malware through evolving techniques to gain persistent access, conduct reconnaissance and collect sensitive geopolitical intelligence.

name: The Chrysalis Backdoor: A Deep Dive into Lotus Blossom’s toolkit
description: Chinese hackers used a previously undocumented custom backdoor to deliver shellcode to victims of a targeted espionage campaign, according to Rapid7 Labs and the Rapid 7 MDR team, who have uncovered a new type of malicious implant.

name: Chinese APT41 Hackers Target Mobile Devices with New WyrmSpy and DragonEgg Spyware
description:
The prolific China-linked nation-state actor known as APT41 has been linked to two previously undocumented strains of Android spyware called WyrmSpy and DragonEgg.

"Known for its exploitation of web-facing applications and infiltration of traditional endpoint devices, an established threat actor like APT 41 including mobile in its arsenal of malware shows how mobile endpoints are high-value targets with coveted corporate and personal data," Lookout said in a report shared with The Hacker News.

APT41, also tracked under the names Axiom, Blackfly, Brass Typhoon (formerly Barium), Bronze Atlas, HOODOO, Wicked Panda, and Winnti, is known to be operational since at least 2007, targeting a wide range of industries to conduct intellectual property theft.

Recent attacks mounted by the adversarial collective have leveraged an open-source red teaming tool known as Google Command and Control (GC2) as part of attacks aimed at media and job platforms in Taiwan and Italy.

name: Volt Typhoon / Bronze Silhouette
description: Microsoft has uncovered stealthy and targeted malicious activity focused on post-compromise credential access and network system discovery aimed at critical infrastructure organizations in the United States. The attack is carried out by Volt Typhoon, a state-sponsored actor based in China that typically focuses on espionage and information gathering. Microsoft assesses with moderate confidence that this Volt Typhoon campaign is pursuing development of capabilities that could disrupt critical communications infrastructure between the United States and Asia region during future crises.

name: Billbug: State-sponsored Actor Targets Cert Authority, Government Agencies in Multiple Asian Countries
description: State-sponsored actors compromised a digital certificate authority in an Asian country during a campaign in which multiple government agencies were also targeted.

name: BRONZE PRESIDENT Targets Government Officials | Secureworks
description: Get started with the help of a company that provides a range of solutions for security problems, as well as a host of other services, on-the-spot and off- the field, in a bid to attract new customers.

name: Flying in the clouds: APT31 renews its attacks on Russian companies through cloud storage - Stealer0x3401 - YaRAT
description: A guide to the latest developments in the fight against cyber-thieves APT31, who are believed to be targeting Russian companies through cloud storage, as well as providing security services for the energy sector.

name: Mustang Panda - New wave of malware targeting Europe
description: Cisco Talos has identified a new wave of malware being deployed by Mustang Panda, a China-based threat actor that has targeted European countries, including Russia, and the United States, since 2012.

name: Reemergence of Chinese "Override Panda" with New Espionage Operations
description: Recently, Override Panda (APT30) has resurfaced with new phishing attack with the goal of stealing sensitive information. The latest campaign spotted by Cluster25 found out that the Override Panda utilizes a Microsoft Office document that includes a loader designed to run a shellcode, which in turn injects a beacon for "Viper". Viper is similar to Cobalt Strike, where it features over 80 modules to facilitate initial access, persistence, privilege escalation, credential access, lateral movement, and arbitrary command execution.

name: HAFNIUM Utilizes Scheduler Task to evade security
description: Microsoft has discovered HAFNIUM new activity by exploiting unpatched zero-day vulnerabilities as entry point. Observed from August 2021 to February 2020, telecommunication, internet service provider and data services sector were the targeted sector. It was found that the malware called Tarrask creates a hidden task scheduler to evade security detection. The threat actor configured this malware with multiple stages. The initial stage is to configure the scheduler task while the goal of the second stage is to set up a communication with C2 server. It’s possible the threat actor wanted to ensure persistence across reboots and therefore chose not to perform those steps, instead deleting only the SD value; however, we also speculate that the threat actor was unaware that the task would continue to run even after these components were removed.
